en: Gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth of Earth's gravity, so a 60-kilogram person weighs only 10 kilograms there.
Light travels at 299,792,458 meters per second in a vacuum, allowing it to circle the Earth about 7.5 times in one second.
A single lightning bolt can reach 30,000 degrees Celsius, which is five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Sound travels through water at about 1,480 meters per second, which is more than four times faster than it travels through air.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal, requiring a massive 3,422 degrees Celsius before it turns into a liquid.
A fully drawn bow stores about 50 joules of elastic potential energy, which transfers to the arrow as kinetic energy when released.
A block and tackle pulley system with four rope segments can lift a 400-newton load using only 100 newtons of force.
A standard car tire has about 1,500 tiny tread blocks that increase friction to stop the vehicle safely on wet roads.
The strongest continuous magnetic field in a laboratory reached 45.5 Tesla, which is about 9,000 times stronger than a standard fridge magnet.
A standard wheelchair ramp has a slope ratio of 1:12, meaning it rises exactly 1 inch for every 12 inches of length.
One dietary Calorie equals 4,184 joules, so eating a 100-Calorie apple gives your body enough energy to lift a 10-kilogram box over 4,000 meters.
To escape Earth's gravity and travel into deep space, a rocket must reach a minimum speed of 11.2 kilometers per second.
